description: Every LightsOut schedule in the cluster. Shows what each schedule manages, how much of it is off right now, and what failed. Built to stay readable with hundreds of schedules.

panels.description: Counts the schedules that are in a down window now. These are the ones currently releasing compute.
panels.title: Schedules Down

panels.description: Counts the schedules that are in an up window now.
panels.title: Schedules Up

panels.description: Counts the schedules that are on the way up but do not serve yet. A schedule warms up while its custom resources come back, or while a sync wave settles.
panels.title: Warming Up

panels.description: Counts the deployments, statefulsets and cronjobs the schedules manage.
panels.title: Workloads Managed

panels.description: Counts the managed workloads that are at zero replicas or suspended right now. This is the number that tracks released compute. A schedule reporting Down while this stays low did not finish its work.
panels.title: Workloads Down Now

panels.description: Counts the operator-managed custom resources the schedules turn off, such as database and broker clusters. This is a gauge, so it reports the current count without waiting for a transition.
panels.title: Custom Resources

panels.description: Counts pods that still run well after their grace period ends. A count above zero means a namespace keeps the compute that the downscale had to release.
panels.title: Stuck Pods

panels.description: Counts the scaling operations that failed inside the dashboard time range. Each operator pod keeps its own counter, so this covers the pods that reported inside the window.
panels.title: Errors

panels.description: How the fleet moves through the day, as three counts rather than one row per schedule. This panel reads the same with ten schedules or a thousand.
panels.title: Schedules by State

panels.description: Only the schedules with something wrong: a failed scaling operation, a pod that will not terminate, or a reconcile older than 10 minutes. An empty panel is the healthy answer.
panels.title: Needs Attention

panels.description: One row per schedule. Each band shows how long the schedule held one state. A yellow band is a schedule that is on the way up but does not serve yet. Narrow the Schedule list above when the fleet is too large to read.
panels.title: Schedule State Over Time

panels.description: One row per schedule, paginated. Select a schedule name to open its detail dashboard.
panels.title: All Schedules

panels.description: The two lines that answer whether the schedules are doing their job. The gap between them is what is still running inside a down window.
panels.title: Workloads Managed and Down

panels.description: How the managed workloads split across deployments, statefulsets and cronjobs, and how many of each are off right now.
panels.title: Workloads by Type

panels.description: Counts the operator-managed custom resources the schedules match, by kind. A kind drops to zero while a delete entry holds its resources down, and comes back when the operator rebuilds them.
panels.title: Custom Resources by Kind

panels.description: Counts the workloads the schedules have scaled, by direction. The counter only moves at a transition, so the line steps rather than slopes. Each operator pod keeps its own counter, so the line steps down when the pod restarts.
panels.title: Scaling Operations (cumulative)

panels.description: How long a full scaling pass takes, over the dashboard time range. Rate limits and sync waves make this longer. The buckets are cumulative, so this covers every pass the current operator pods have run.
panels.title: Scaling Duration

panels.description: Counts the custom resource operations the schedules have run, by kind. The workload_type label holds the kind, so any value other than Deployment, StatefulSet or CronJob names a custom resource.
panels.title: Custom Resource Operations by Kind (cumulative)

panels.description: The namespaces holding pods that outlived their grace period after a downscale. Those pods keep their nodes alive while the schedule reports Down. An empty panel is the healthy answer.
panels.title: Stuck Terminating Pods

panels.description: Counts the workloads the scaling passes have handled, by result. A failure line that climbs is the first sign that a downscale is only half done. Each operator pod keeps its own counter, so the line steps down when the pod restarts.
panels.title: Workloads Processed by Result (cumulative)
